slides.display_title: The Economic and Structural Reality of Modern Healthcare
slides.visual_description: The Economic and Structural Reality of Modern Healthcare — Explain how rising national health expenditures and the shift from independent practice to hospital or large-system employment change the context in which physicians must operate and influence care.
slides.script_notes: The Economic and Structural Reality of Modern Healthcare — Explain how rising national health expenditures and the shift from independent practice to hospital or large-system employment change the context in which physicians must operate and influence care.

slides.display_title: The Human Cost of System Waste and Administrative Burden
slides.visual_description: The Human Cost of System Waste and Administrative Burden — Describe how administrative waste and bureaucratic tasks contribute to inefficiency and physician burnout, and interpret burnout as a system design problem rather than an individual resilience problem.
slides.script_notes: The Human Cost of System Waste and Administrative Burden — Describe how administrative waste and bureaucratic tasks contribute to inefficiency and physician burnout, and interpret burnout as a system design problem rather than an individual resilience problem.

slides.display_title: The Knowledge Explosion and Emerging Technologies
slides.visual_description: The Knowledge Explosion and Emerging Technologies — Summarize how rapid medical knowledge growth, expanding AI use, and selected digital training and monitoring tools are reshaping care delivery and clinician responsibilities.
slides.script_notes: The Knowledge Explosion and Emerging Technologies — Summarize how rapid medical knowledge growth, expanding AI use, and selected digital training and monitoring tools are reshaping care delivery and clinician responsibilities.

slides.display_title: The Consumer Shift and the Digital Front Door
slides.visual_description: The Consumer Shift and the Digital Front Door — Explain how changing patient expectations for transparency, convenience, and digital access require intentional redesign of the patient journey through tools such as a digital front door.
slides.script_notes: The Consumer Shift and the Digital Front Door — Explain how changing patient expectations for transparency, convenience, and digital access require intentional redesign of the patient journey through tools such as a digital front door.

slides.display_title: The Leadership Gap and the Need for Clinical Innovators
slides.visual_description: The Leadership Gap and the Need for Clinical Innovators — Interpret the gap between physicians’ interest in leadership and their limited formal business or executive training, and explain why clinicians must bridge practice, business, and technology strategy.
slides.script_notes: The Leadership Gap and the Need for Clinical Innovators — Interpret the gap between physicians’ interest in leadership and their limited formal business or executive training, and explain why clinicians must bridge practice, business, and technology strategy.

slides.display_title: Synthesis: Why Incremental Adaptation Is No Longer Enough
slides.visual_description: Synthesis: Why Incremental Adaptation Is No Longer Enough — Synthesize the lesson’s major forces—economic, structural, human, technological, and consumer-driven—into a concise case for deliberate leadership in shaping future care delivery.
slides.script_notes: Synthesis: Why Incremental Adaptation Is No Longer Enough — Synthesize the lesson’s major forces—economic, structural, human, technological, and consumer-driven—into a concise case for deliberate leadership in shaping future care delivery.
